hints: Look closely at what label 1 is bracketing on the right side, a branched sugar chain on top joined to a large oval sitting in the top layer, and look at where label 2 points on the bottom layer.
Remember the naming rule: sugar joined to protein makes one type of conjugate, sugar joined to lipid makes another, and the round parts of the bilayer are the hydrophilic phosphate heads.
walkthrough:
**Decode label 1**

Look at the right side of the diagram. You can see hexagon shapes sticking out of the membrane. Those are carbohydrate chains. They are attached to a big oval protein embedded in the membrane.

Carbohydrate + protein = glycoprotein.

**Decode label 2**

Label 2 points to one of the small circles at the bottom of the bilayer. The bilayer is made of phospholipids, and each phospholipid has a round hydrophilic head and two wiggly hydrophobic tails.

So that small circle is a phosphate head.

**Match to the table**

1 is glycoprotein and 2 is phosphate head. That is row C. Well done, this is classic fluid mosaic model recognition.

options.A: 1 is correctly a glycoprotein, but 2 is not a whole protein. It is just the small round phosphate head of a phospholipid in the bilayer.
options.B: Both parts are wrong. 1 is attached to a protein, not a lipid, so it is not a glycolipid, and 2 is a phosphate head, not a lipoprotein.
options.C: Correct. 1 shows carbohydrate attached to an extrinsic protein, a glycoprotein, and 2 shows the hydrophilic phosphate head of a bilayer phospholipid.
options.D: 2 is correctly a phosphate head, but 1 is not a glycolipid. The carbohydrate is joined to a large protein, so it is a glycoprotein.
